manualSemanticReview.reviewer: Codex manual reading of all saved answers, recipient copy, claim ledgers and exact quotes, with actual mobile screenshot inspection; not independent human assessment
manualSemanticReview.summary: All twelve prompts returned accepted turns and 69/70 mechanical checks passed. Semantic acceptance still failed: the office report became an unlabeled fact, content-bearing text bypassed the ledger as style, some identifiers were not covered by their cited quotes, and SMS selected an older artifact. These failures require correction and fresh qualification.

findings.result: Both Why variants respond without clarification. Longer Why links the missing note to preparing follow-up; the shorter Why still mixes payer-boundary boilerplate into its reason.

Exact source passages are available and expand correctly, but the direct answer generically names workflow/governed sources rather than identifying the notice/inventory and quoting the relevant passage. Partial, not full semantic acceptance.

Email is unsent and excludes labeled owner/permission fields but includes internal case-controls wording. Warmer shortening meets the word ceiling and lineage; its content-bearing body and subject were incorrectly labeled style with no claims. The phrase about moving forward on the recipient behalf lacks specific support.

Handoff carries the right prior artifact and missing note. SMS has no specific restricted details and fits 250 characters, but references the warmer email rather than the latest handoff; the mechanical SMS check did not test this lineage.

Recorded interaction uses uncited style and omits unverified in the answer. Recall and summary assert the report as fact while citing unrelated workflow/document quotes. The reviewer borrowed the uncited report from full context and approved both. No authoritative workflow record was changed.

findings.breakdown: Seven claims include a request ID absent from their own quotes; three of these also assert receipt absent from their quote. Two claims assert an office communication without a conversation citation or unverified label. Additional material content outside the ledger occurs in turns 7 and 10, so a ledger-only unsupported rate understates the problem.
findings.limitation: Small repeated synthetic sample; neither positive model review nor an exact quote establishes entailment.

findings.result: No premature dependency-completion claims, conversation effects or decisions. All strict actual-viewport, composer, overflow, source expansion, compaction and feedback checks passed. Manual 375x812 screenshot confirms the lead and composer are visible.

limitations: The frozen prompts are developer-authored and repeatedly used; no independent holdout or human study.
Earlier failures and the unsuccessful transport traces remain immutable.
The separate current-runtime boundary run is still pending.
Neutral style restrictions, claim-scoped review input, visible memory requirements and explicit active-artifact context are subsequent local corrections, not evidence that this run passed.

caveats: Exact twelve-prompt core comparison; developer-authored synthetic conversation, not an independent holdout.
Mechanical checks do not prove natural-language entailment or response usefulness; semantic review is separate.
Old bodies include their template subject and internal metadata; each shortening ratio compares that arm’s own body field.
Latency is end-to-end browser submission to saved display, including service/network effects. Cache and free-service cold starts may differ.

Reported generation requests/tokens exclude embedding usage and unreported failed-request tokens. A conservative September 9, 2026 estimate uses $0.40/M input and $1.60/M output, ignoring cache discounts; not a billing record.
The earlier boundary continuation is a reference trace; the new boundary scenario is separately isolated. Only the core is presented as an exact conversational pair.
